Rashi on Nazir 28a:11:1.english: An unsightly wife - Who does not drink wine.

Rashi on Nazir 28a:12:1.hebrew: דאי ר"א - כיון דתגלחת מעכבתה שלא לשתות יין, כדאמרינן בפרק ג' מינין (לקמן נזיר דף מו.): "ואחר ישתה הנזיר יין" — אחר מעשים כולן, דברי ר"א. הילכך, כיון דלא גילחה — אסורה ביין, והוה לה ניוול, כדכתיב (זכריה ט׳:י״ז): "ותירוש ינובב בתולות". הילכך, מצי מפר, אע"פ שנזרקו עליה כל הדמים:
Rashi on Nazir 28a:12:1.english: For if Rabbi Eliezer - Since [the requirement of] shaving holds her back from drinking wine, as we say in the chapter [entitled] Sheloshah Minim (below, Nazir 46a): “And after that the nazirite may drink wine” — after all the actions [are completed], [these are] the words of Rabbi Eliezer. Therefore, since she has not shaved, she is forbidden [to drink] wine, and she suffers disfigurement, as it is written (Zechariah 9:17): “And new wine makes maidens flourish.” Therefore, he can nullify [her vow], even though all the blood was sprinkled for her:

Rashi on Nazir 28a:1:1.hebrew: בזמן שהן סתומין - כדתנן בשילהי מתני':
Rashi on Nazir 28a:1:1.english: When they are unallocated - As we learned at the end of the Mishnah.

Rashi on Nazir 28a:1:2.hebrew: ת"ל - "ואם כבש יביא קרבנו" — בקרבנו יוצא כו'. ואית דדרשי ליה מקרבנו קמא:
Rashi on Nazir 28a:1:2.english: The verse states - “And if he brings a lamb for his offering” [Leviticus 4:32] — with his offering he fulfills [his obligation], etc. And there are those who derive it from the earlier [mention of] “his offering” [Leviticus 4:28].

Rashi on Nazir 28a:2:1.english: From a minor [transgression] for a minor [transgression] - From an oath of testimony to an oath of deposit or to an oath of utterance.

Rashi on Nazir 28a:2:2.hebrew: מן החמורה על החמורה - מחלב לדם, מחייבי מיתות לחייבי כריתות בשוגג:
Rashi on Nazir 28a:2:2.english: From a major [transgression] to a major [transgression] - From [forbidden] fat to blood, [or] from [sins] punishable by death to [sins] punishable by excision, [committed] inadvertently.

Rashi on Nazir 28a:4:1.hebrew: שכן אם הפריש בהמה על - החלב שאכל בשוגג, והביאה על הדם שאכל בשוגג:
Rashi on Nazir 28a:4:1.english: For if he separated an animal for - The [forbidden] fat that he ate unintentionally, and brought it for the blood that he ate unintentionally.

Rashi on Nazir 28a:4:2.hebrew: שהרי לא מעל - לפי שהוא קדושת הגוף, ואי אפשר לו להוציאה לחולין, לפיכך לא כיפר. וכדאמרי' בפרק [בתרא] דכריתות, דכיון דלא מצי מעיל — כפורי נמי לא מכפר:
Rashi on Nazir 28a:4:2.english: For he has not misused [it] - Because it has inherent sanctity, and it is impossible for him to transfer it to non-sacred status, therefore it did not effect atonement. And as we say in the [last] chapter of Keritot, that since he cannot commit misuse, it also does not effect atonement.

Rashi on Nazir 28a:4:3.hebrew: שהרי מעל וכפר - דכיון דלקח בהן חטאת אחר שלא הופרש לשמן, הוה ליה כמפיק להו לחולין ומעל. וכיון דמעל בו, אמרי' "וכפר", דהוא קרבן מעליא:
Rashi on Nazir 28a:4:3.english: For he has misused [consecrated property] and it atoned - For since he purchased with them another sin-offering, for which [the money] was not designated, he is considered as having removed them to non-sacred status, and he has committed misuse. And since he committed misuse with it, we say “and it atoned,” for it is a proper offering.

Rashi on Nazir 28a:7:1.hebrew: ת"ל - וכפר עליו הכהן על חטאתו — דלעולם לא כפר עד שיהא קרבנו לשום חטאו, שאע"פ שמעל לא כיפר. שהרי מעל במעות — כל דבר שיוצא לחולין אית ביה מעילה, והואיל דאית ביה מעילה, כיפר:
Rashi on Nazir 28a:7:1.english: The verse states - “And the priest shall make atonement for him regarding his sin” — that [an offering] never atones unless his offering is for the sake of his [specific] sin, so that even though he committed *me’ilah*, it did not atone. For [as to the premise that] he committed *me’ilah* with the money: anything that goes out to non-sacred status is subject to *me’ilah*, and since it is subject to *me’ilah*, [one might have thought that] it atoned.

Rashi on Nazir 28a:8:1.hebrew: קתני מיהת בהמה - שהרי אין אדם מגלח על בהמת אביו. מאי טעמא? לאו משום דכמפורשת דמיא? מאי לאו, אפי' בעלת מום:
Rashi on Nazir 28a:8:1.english: In any event, it teaches [the case of] an animal - For a person does not shave on his father's animal. What is the reason? Is it not because it is considered like [funds that are] allocated? What, is it not [referring] even to a blemished [animal]?

Rashi on Nazir 28a:9:1.english: Why does [the baraita] specifically teach - [In the clause:] “However, he fulfills [his obligation] with money that [his father] separated,” etc.

Tosafot on Nazir 28a:10:1.hebrew: נזרק עליה אחד מן הדמים - כגון שגמרה נזירות בטהרה, והביאה קרבנות נזירות טהרה — שהן ג' בהמות: כבשה לחטאת, וכבש לעולה, ואיל לשלמים — ונזרק עליה אחד מן הדמים, חטאת או עולה או שלמים, אינו יכול להפר נדרה לענין שלא תצטרך לגלח ולהביא שאר קרבנות. דלפי שאין כאן עוד עינוי נפש, דביין מותרת. ואי משום שצריכה לגלח, ומטו עליה "אשה מתגלחת" — אפשר לה בפאה נכרית; הכי מפרש בגמרא. אבל אי לא נזרק הדם עדיין, דאסורה [ביין] — מיקרי שפיר עינוי נפש, אע"ג דלא מיתסרא אלא שעתא פורתא:
Tosafot on Nazir 28a:10:1.english: If the blood of one of them was sprinkled on her behalf - For example, where she completed [her] naziriteship in purity and brought the offerings of naziriteship of purity — which are three animals: an ewe-lamb for a sin-offering, a ram-lamb for a burnt-offering, and a ram for a peace-offering — and the blood of one of them, [whether] the sin-offering, the burnt-offering, or the peace-offering, was sprinkled on her behalf, [the husband] cannot nullify her vow such that she would not need to shave and bring the remaining offerings. For there is no longer any affliction of the soul here, as she is permitted to drink wine. And if [one might suggest that he can nullify] because she must shave, and they apply to her [the complaint regarding] "a woman who shaves" — she can [wear] a wig; so the Gemara explains. However, if the blood was not yet sprinkled, so that she is forbidden [to drink wine], it is rightly called an affliction of the soul, even though she is forbidden for only a short time.

Tosafot on Nazir 28a:10:2.hebrew: רבי עקיבא אומר אפילו נשחט - ולא נזרק הדם — אינו יכול להפר. בגמרא מפרש: משום הפסד קדשים. ומסיק בגמרא: כשנשחטה החטאת; שאם יפר לה, נמצאת בהמה זו תצא לבית השריפה, שהיא אינה צריכה לחטאת, וגם לא יוכל לזרוק דמה לשם שלמים, דחטאת שלא לשמה פסולה. יש להסתפק: אם היפר לה — אם מופר, או שמא יש כח ביד חכמים לעקור דבר מן התורה בשב ואל תעשה:
Tosafot on Nazir 28a:10:2.english: Rabbi Akiva says: Even [if] it was slaughtered - And the blood was not [yet] sprinkled, he cannot nullify [her vow]. In the Gemara [it] explains: Because of the loss of consecrated property. And the Gemara concludes: When the sin-offering was slaughtered; for if he nullifies [the vow] for her, it turns out that this animal will go out to the place of burning, since she does not need a sin-offering, and he also cannot sprinkle its blood for the sake of a peace-offering, for a sin-offering [offered] not for its own sake is invalid. There is room to question: If he did nullify [it] for her, is it nullified, or perhaps the Sages have the power to uproot a matter from the Torah through "sit and do not act"?

Tosafot on Nazir 28a:11:1.hebrew: בד"א - שאינו יכול להפר אחר שנזרק אחד מן הדמים, בתגלחת טהרה — כדפי' שגמרה נזירות בטהרה. אבל בתגלחת טומאה, כגון שנטמאת בנזירותה והביאה קרבנותיה בטומאה, אע"פ שנזרקו דמים — יכול להפר, מפני שאפשר לומר לה: "אי אפשי באשה מנוולת", כלומר שהיא צריכה למנות מעתה נזירות טהרה ותאסר ביין, ויש כאן עינוי נפש. וה"נ בגמרא מצינו לשון ניוול שר"ל עינוי. וקשה לישנא (דעינוי) ד"אי אפשי", דהוי ליה למימר "משום עינוי"! וצ"ל דקאי אדר"ע, דקאמר: שנשחטה אחת מן הבהמות אינו יכול להפר, מפני שאפשר [לבוא] להפסד קדשים; אע"ג דאסורה ביין עד שישחטו שאר הבהמות ויזרוק דמן, ויש כאן ענוי נפש פורתא — בשביל ההוא פורתא אינו יכול להפר בשביל הפסד קדשים. אבל בתגלחת דטומאה, דאיכא עינוי נפש גדול, שסותרת ובעי למימני נזירות אחרת — [מודה] שיכול לומר לה: "אי אפשי [בעינוי] גדול". א"נ, משום דר"מ קאמר האי לישנא "אי איפשי", קאמר ת"ק נמי "אי אפשי":
Tosafot on Nazir 28a:11:1.english: "In what [case] is this said?" — That he cannot nullify [the vow] after the blood of one of [the offerings] was sprinkled [applies only] to the shaving of purity, as we explained, where she completed [her] naziriteship in purity. But regarding the shaving of impurity, such as where she became ritually impure during her naziriteship and brought her offerings for [her] impurity, even though the blood was sprinkled, he can nullify [the vow], because it is possible [for him] to say to her: "I do not want an unkempt wife" — that is to say, that from now on she must count a naziriteship of purity and will be forbidden to [drink] wine, and there is an affliction of the soul [innui nefesh] here. And so too, in the Gemara we find the expression nivvul [unkemptness], which means affliction. And the phrasing ([of affliction]) "I do not want" is difficult, for it should have said "because of affliction"! And one must say that it refers to [the view of] Rabbi Akiva, who said [that once] one of the animals has been slaughtered, he cannot nullify [the vow], because it is possible [to lead] to a loss of consecrated items; even though she is forbidden to [drink] wine until the rest of the animals are slaughtered and their blood is sprinkled, and there is a small affliction of the soul here, [yet] on account of that small [affliction] he cannot nullify [the vow] because of the loss of consecrated items. But regarding the shaving of impurity, where there is great affliction of the soul — since she forfeits [the days she already observed] and needs to count another naziriteship — [Rabbi Akiva concedes] that he can say to her: "I do not want a great [affliction]." Alternatively, because Rabbi Meir uses this phrasing, "I do not want [a shaven wife]," the first Tanna also says, "I do not want [an unkempt wife]."

Tosafot on Nazir 28a:11:2.hebrew: ה"ג אי אפשי באשה מגלחת - שצריכה לגלח בסוף נזירות טהרה, כדכתיב בהדיא. ולת"ק — אפשר בפאה נכרית; הכי מפרש בגמרא:
Tosafot on Nazir 28a:11:2.english: This is the correct reading: "I do not want a shaven wife" - For she must shave at the conclusion of [her] naziriteship of purity, as is explicitly written. And according to the First Tanna, it is possible [to resolve this] with a wig; so [the Gemara] explains in the Gemara.

Tosafot on Nazir 28a:12:1.hebrew: תגלחת מעכבת - מלשתות ביין. וכיון דאי לא גילחה אסורה, ואית לה ניוול — פי' צער עינוי נפש, שצריכה להיות מעונה מן היין עד שתגלח — מצי מיפר, בעבור ההיא שעתא פורתא דאסירה ביין:
Tosafot on Nazir 28a:12:1.english: "Shaving is indispensable" - [That it prevents her] from drinking wine. And since, if she has not shaved, she is forbidden [from wine] and suffers degradation [nivvul] — meaning, the pain of affliction of the soul [innui nefesh], in that she must be afflicted [by abstaining] from wine until she shaves — he can nullify [the vow], on account of that brief time that she is forbidden [to drink] wine.

Tosafot on Nazir 28a:2:1.hebrew: אבל יוצא בקרבן שהפריש לעצמו - לעבירה זו, ויביאנו לעבירה אחרת:
Tosafot on Nazir 28a:2:1.english: "However, he fulfills [his obligation] with an offering he separated for himself" - [That is, he separated it] for this transgression, and he would bring it for another transgression.

Tosafot on Nazir 28a:4:1.hebrew: שהרי לא מעל - בשוגג, אם שגג והקריב קרבן על הדם שהוא קרבן של חלב — דאכתי בקדושתייהו קאי, כיון דבהמה קדושה קדושת הגוף, ולא נפק לחולין בהכי, כיון שלא נהנה ממנה; "לא כיפר" — במזיד, דלא עשה כלום, שאינו יכול להתכפר בקרבן של דם כלל? אלא: לא מעל — אם עשה (בו) בשוגג, הואיל ואינו מוציאו מרשות הקדש אלא מהקדש זה להקדש אחר, ומתוך שלא מעל — לא כיפר. והכי מפרש ליה בפרק בתרא דכריתות (דף כז:). ואחרי שאנו רואין בשוגג דלא כיפר, דין הוא כשנתכוון לעקר חטאת חלב ולעשות חטאת דם — דלא כיפר:
Tosafot on Nazir 28a:4:1.english: "For he has not misused [consecrated property]" - [Lest one suggest that this means: "He has not misused"] in the case of inadvertence — if he erred and sacrificed an offering for [consuming] blood [that was designated as] an offering for [eating forbidden] fat — for it still remains in its consecrated status, since an animal is holy with bodily sanctity and does not become secular through this, since he derived no benefit from it; [and] "and did not atone" [refers to] an intentional act — for he accomplished nothing, as he cannot atone with an offering for blood at all? [Rather:] "He has not misused" — if he acted [with it] inadvertently, since he does not remove it from the domain of consecrated property, but only [transfers it] from this consecrated status to another consecrated status; and because he did not misuse consecrated property, it did not atone. And so [the Gemara] explains it in the final chapter of Keritot (27b). And after we see that in the case of inadvertence it does not atone, it is logical [all the more so] that when he intentionally intended to uproot a fat sin-offering and make [it] a blood sin-offering, that it does not atone.

Tosafot on Nazir 28a:7:1.hebrew: על חטאתו - וכפר הכהן על חטאתו בכבשה דיחיד כתיב, אלמא דבמזיד אינו יכול לשנות, אפי' במעות. וכן תניא בתוספתא דכריתות [פ"ד]: הפריש מעות לחטאת חלב והביאום על חטאת דם, לחטאת דם והביאום לחטאת חלב — בשוגג מעל, לפיכך כיפר; במזיד לא מעל, לפיכך לא כיפר. [אלמא] במזיד אף במעות לא כיפר, וכ"ש בהמה דלא מצי משנה. ולפי' זו התוספתא משמע דנסיבא קרא אחרינא "על חטאתו", ולא פסוק ראשון שדרש כבר. ה"ג: "שהרי מעל וכפר" — שהמעות אין בהם קדושת הגוף ויוצאין מקדושתן בקל, וכשמשנה אותו לקרבן אחר נפקי המעות לחולין, והרי הן חולין ביד מוכר הבהמה, דאי לא נפקא לחולין לא מעל, ולכך נמי כפר בשוגג. ולכך במזיד נמי נימא דכפר, הואיל ושייך בהו שנוי; בשוגג אמר "ומעל וכיפר", ולא במזיד. ומיהו אי לא הוה ילפי' [קרא ה"א]: מזיד וכפר. אע"ג שדרשנו "וכפר על חטאתו" — עד שיהא קרבנו לשם חטאתו, תרתי שמעינן מיניה, כדאמרינן בעלמא (גיטין דף נב.): "אתם" — ולא שותפין, "אתם" — ולא אפוטרופסים, "אתם" — ולא התורם את שאינו שלו, וכולהון דרשינן מחד "אתם":
Tosafot on Nazir 28a:7:1.english: "For his sin" - "And the priest shall make atonement for his sin" (Leviticus 4:35) is written regarding the female sheep of an individual [brought as a sin-offering], which shows that intentionally one cannot change [the offering's designation], even with money. And similarly it is taught in the Tosefta of Keritot [ch. 4]: [If] one separated money for a sin-offering of [forbidden] fat and they brought them for a sin-offering of blood, [or if he separated money] for a sin-offering of blood and they brought them for a sin-offering of fat — [if done] inadvertently (beshogeg), he has committed trespass (me'ilah), therefore it has atoned; [if done] intentionally (bemezid), he has not committed trespass, therefore it has not atoned. [Consequently,] intentionally, even with money it does not atone, and all the more so [with an] animal, that he cannot change [its designation]. And according to the explanation of this Tosefta, it implies that it cites another verse of "for his sin", and not the first verse that it already expounded. This is the correct reading: "For he has committed trespass and it has atoned" — for money does not have intrinsic sanctity (sanctity of the body) and departs from its sanctity easily; and when he diverts it to another offering, the money exits to non-sacred status and is non-sacred in the hands of the seller of the animal, for if it did not exit to non-sacred status he would not have committed trespass, and for this reason it also atoned in the case of inadvertence. And for this reason, let us say that in the case of intentional [diversion] as well it should atone, since substitution applies to them [i.e., money]; [though] in the case of inadvertence [the Baraita] stated "he committed trespass and it atoned", but not in the case of intentional [diversion]. However, if we had not derived [it from a verse, I would have said]: [even] intentionally it atoned. [And] even though we [already] derived "and [the priest] shall make atonement for his sin" [to mean] that his offering must be for the sake of his sin, we learn two [teachings] from it, just as we say elsewhere (Gittin 52a): "'You' — and not partners; 'you' — and not guardians; 'you' — and not one who separates terumah from that which is not his" — and all of them we derive from a single "you":

Tosafot on Nazir 28a:8:1.hebrew: קתני מיהא - לעיל, דאינו מגלח על בהמת אביו, מאי לאו אפילו בעלת מום? אלמא כמפורשין דמיין; דאי כסתומין — לגלח, כמו על מעות סתומין. ומדמי הילכתא: דה"ה דלענין אותה ההלכה נתקבלה דמעות סתומין יפלו לנדבה, נימא דוקא מעות ולא בהמה, ואפילו בעלת מום. וליכא למידחי דהא דקתני לעיל דאינו מגלח על בהמת אביו היינו במפורשין — דאם כן, היכי מסיק: "אבל יוצא במעות אביו, שהרי מגלח על מעות אביו"? והא אין מגלח אלא על מעות סתומין של אביו, כדקתני בהדיא במתניתין (לקמן נזיר דף ל.):
Tosafot on Nazir 28a:8:1.english: "In any event, it teaches" - Above, [where the baraita teaches] that [a person] does not shave using his father's animal: what, is it not even a blemished [animal]? Consequently, [animals] are considered like allocated [funds]; for if [they were considered] like unallocated [funds], let him shave [using them], just like with unallocated money! And [the Gemara] equates the halakhot: that the same applies regarding that halakha that was received [as a tradition], that unallocated money falls to freewill-offerings — let us say [it means] specifically money and not an animal, even a blemished one. And one cannot deflect [the objection by arguing] that that which was taught above, that he does not shave using his father's animal, refers to allocated [animals] — for if so, how could [the baraita] conclude: "However, he fulfills [his obligation] with his father's money, for he may shave using his father's money"? But surely he may shave only using his father's unallocated money, as is taught explicitly in our Mishnah (below, Nazir 30a)!

Tosafot on Nazir 28a:8:2.hebrew: לא תמימים - עליהם אינו מגלח, דהויא כמפורשים:
Tosafot on Nazir 28a:8:2.english: "No, unblemished" - [It is] with them that he may not shave, as it is considered like allocated [funds].
